description:
GH #296 family on develop f822f0f84 (debug, opt-level 1), scratch scratchpad/m296 (gen.py, measure.sh, analyze.py, out/). A main body of N computed tuple elements or N sequential calls: product requests are linear (largest drive about 7N + 432 for tuples, 12.2N for seq), but interp wall time grows with exponent 1.9 to 2.0 (tuple 400 -> 1000: 1.86, 1000 -> 2000: 1.97; seq 1000 -> 2000: 1.99).
Where (work_graph.applied completions, each charged the gap since the previous event; an attribution, not a profile), jobs on main's one body:
  DeriveRuntimeDemand   tuple400 40 ms, tuple1000 238 ms, tuple2000 918 ms
  LowerFunction         28 ms, 167 ms, 673 ms
  AnalyzeActivation     18 ms, 99 ms, 367 ms
Doubling N multiplies each by about 3.9. One callsite.defined event takes up to 197 ms; the ten slowest are 969 of the 977 ms charged to that name. The 3-request reach drive takes about 500 ms at N=1000 and 2.0 s at N=2000. pull.product.evaluated is cheap (63 ms for 7.5k, 226 ms for 14.5k).
Not investigated: the loop inside each job. Known per-step suspects from earlier work: callsite_returns_feeding scans every callsite per return (runtime_demand.rs), per-entry capture demand publication. A sample of interp on tuple2000 names the frames.
Fails before, passes after: a telemetry test pins that each of the three jobs' work on a body of N calls grows linearly (a count of steps visited, not time).
Acceptance: full gate green; no pin rises unexplained.
Sampled (macOS sample, 1 ms, main thread; tuple1000 vs tuple2000 on fz2-develop; scratch scratchpad/jxo/ s1000.txt, s2000.txt, agg.py, incl.py). Total samples 1593 -> 3102. Superlinear self-time leaves, N=1000 -> 2000:
- AnalyzeActivation (inclusive 311 -> 2804): semantic::entry_scope 97 -> 957; BTreeMap<ValueId, Ty>::insert 85 -> 605; merge_value_types 211 at N=2000. Per-step rebuild or merge of a value-type map that grows with the body.
- Job completion (complete_job, inclusive 328 -> 1292): FactKey::eq 145 -> 374, CallSiteKey::eq 100 -> 517, slice_contains over DependencyKeys 33 -> 190, OrderedSet<DependencyKey>::insert 17 -> 105. Dependency dedup by linear scan.
- DeriveRuntimeDemand (inclusive 218 -> 752): runtime_demand::callsite_returns_feeding 39 -> 400.
- LowerFunction (0 samples at N=1000, an unexplained gap; 917 at N=2000): origin_source_path 248, origin_may_retain_source 147, value_may_retain_source 132 — the same tuple-retention walk fz-1y9 described for nested pairs.
- Drop of RawTable<ControlEntryId, RuntimeDemand> 23 -> 117; Vec<Option<RuntimeDemand>> resize/clone spread across jobs.
So there is no one shared leaf: four separate per-step scans over a growing body. Open: why LowerFunction has no samples at N=1000 (resample).
title: The per-body jobs on one long body cost time linear in its length
